_readme: TWO PASSES, IN ORDER. Pass 1 is `inventory` — what is this source even about.
Pass 2 is `dimensions` — is it good enough to build from. Do not start pass 2 until
every inventory row is filled: a grade over a corpus you have not identified is a
grade of your own assumptions.
INVENTORY (pass 1), one row per file — EVERY file under sourceRoot, no format skipped —
filled by OPENING it:
kind:        docs | code | data | ui | contract | unknown
answers:     which dimension keys this source can speak to, e.g. ["domain","rules"].
Empty list is a real answer — say so rather than leaving it null.
statedScope: if the source declares its own boundary, quote it VERBATIM. Sources
that say what they do not cover are the cheapest scope signal there is.
components:  named modules/components/aggregates this source defines, one string each.
format/route/media/pages are stamped by init from bin/lib/source-formats.tsv — what the
file is by extension, the extraction route that consumes it whole, and how
many embedded images/diagrams a text-only read would leave behind. A row
with media > 0 is not consumed until its disposition accounts for them.
DISPOSITIONS (Stage 1) — one entry per inventory row (or a glob covering several), read
by bin/source-ledger.sh, which blocks the Stage 1 and 2 gates while any row has none:
{"path": "<rel>" | "pattern": "<glob over rel>", "state": "extracted",
"artifact": "<project-relative file or dir that carries what was extracted>",
"evidence": "<one specific finding that came OUT of the file, and where it landed>",
"media": <images described, must equal the row's media count, or "mediaWaived": "why">,
"by": "who", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
The artifact must exist, be non-empty, and NAME the source file — a disposition that
says 'the triage already used it' is checked by grepping the triage for the file, and
fails if it never mentions it. Write them with: bin/source-ledger.sh mark ...
A file deliberately not extracted is a register line, not a disposition:
bin/gate-check.sh <project> --waive source/<rel> --reason "..."
DIMENSIONS (pass 2). Fill in every dimension by READING the sources. Do not infer a
rating from file size.
rating: absent | named | specified | verified
evidence: where you saw it (page, section, screen) — or why you concluded absent.
consequence: what the BUILD has to invent if this stays as-is. Be concrete.
Leave rating null for any dimension you did not actually check; the report will
refuse to score rather than treat unchecked as absent.

actors.demands: Who uses the system, and where one role's authority stops
actors.evidence: res.groups records in each addon's security/*_security.xml: Sales User (own docs) / User (all docs) / Administrator; Purchase User/Administrator; Inventory User/Administrator; Invoicing/Billing/Accountant; base Internal/Portal/Public user. implied_ids give the hierarchy.
actors.consequence: Nothing to invent; Stage 3 maps groups to Mendix module/user roles. Portal and public users are out of scope (no portal addon).

domain.demands: Entities, their attributes, and the relationships between them
domain.evidence: ORM models are the executable definition: ~300 _name models across 13 addons (base/models/res_partner.py, product/models/product_template.py, sale/models/sale_order.py, stock/models/stock_move.py, account/models/account_move.py ...), fields with types, required, relations, _inherit/_inherits.
domain.consequence: Nothing missing, the opposite: too much. Stage 3 must simplify (Odoo-inspired, Mendix-native) — choose which of ~300 models become entities; ~95 transient wizards become non-persistent entities or pages.

processes.demands: Flows and sequences: what happens after what, and what state it leaves behind
processes.evidence: State machines as fields.Selection 'state' + action_* methods: sale.order (draft→sent→sale, cancel), purchase.order (draft RFQ→sent→to approve→purchase→done/cancel), stock.picking (draft→waiting→confirmed→assigned→done), account.move (draft→posted→cancel). Bridges sale_stock/purchase_stock create pickings on confirm; stock_account values moves.
processes.consequence: Flow is in Python method bodies, not declared: the extractor can list states and action methods, but the sequence and side effects need reading per method (Stage 1/2). Approval steps (purchase 'to approve' double validation) are candidates for Mendix workflows.

rules.demands: Business rules, validations, thresholds, calculations, eligibility criteria
rules.evidence: @api.depends computes (amounts, taxes, qty_delivered/invoiced), @api.constrains, _sql_constraints, onchanges, pricelist rules (product.pricelist.item), tax computation (account/models/account_tax.py), reservation strategy (stock FIFO/removal).
rules.consequence: Rules are complete but often generic/framework-heavy (account_tax._compute_taxes_for_single_line etc.). For a POC, Stage 2 must pick a simplified rule set (e.g. one tax per line, price-included flag) and record it as a deliberate simplification.

ui.demands: Screens, navigation, layout, and which data appears on which
ui.evidence: 176 views/*.xml + wizard/report xml: form/list/kanban/search/pivot/graph views per model, menuitem trees per app (Sales, Purchase, Inventory, Invoicing), actions with domains/contexts.
ui.consequence: Screens are specified as Odoo views, not wireframes; Stage 3 design must translate them into Mendix pages (Atlas) rather than replicate Odoo's web client. Kanban/pivot need Mendix-native equivalents or are dropped.

integrations.demands: External systems, protocols, credentials, and behaviour when they fail
integrations.evidence: Controllers (portal, download docs), mail templates (data/mail_template_data.xml), payment providers (account_payment, not imported), EDI/e-invoicing hooks in account_move_send.py, barcode nomenclature (not imported).
integrations.consequence: All out of POC scope; the build stubs or omits them. Email sending of quotes/invoices, online payment and portal are declared not implemented.

nfr.demands: Security, performance, availability, retention, data volumes
nfr.evidence: No performance, availability, retention or volume statements anywhere in the code or manifests; only implicit indexes (index=True) and record rules.
nfr.consequence: POC: nothing to invent beyond Mendix defaults. Record as an explicit non-goal rather than a gap.

tenancy.demands: Whether one deployment serves many organisations, and how their data is isolated
tenancy.evidence: Multi-company is pervasive: company_id fields, _check_company_auto, ir.rule records with company_ids in */security/*.xml.
tenancy.consequence: Multi-company is out of scope (confirmed scope); the build uses a single company. Fields company_id are dropped or kept as a single Core.Company reference — Stage 3 decision.

security_model.demands: The actor-to-permission mapping: who may do each thing, and who may not
security_model.evidence: security/ir.model.access.csv per addon (model × group × CRUD) plus ir.rule record rules (e.g. sale 'Personal Orders' rule restricting salesman to own orders).
security_model.consequence: Directly mappable to Mendix entity access + XPath constraints; the extractor should parse the CSVs and rules.

data_migration.demands: Existing data, its volume and shape, and how cutover happens
data_migration.evidence: Only demo/seed data: demo/*.xml, data/template/*-generic_coa.csv (generic chart of accounts, taxes), uom/product categories in data/*.xml. No production data — Odoo here is a reference, not a system being retired.
data_migration.consequence: No data migration (POC, intake Q2/Q5). Seed data (UoM, currencies, chart of accounts, taxes) is reused as Mendix demo/startup data.
